editorial:
Imagine being stuck in a nightmare where the people supposed to protect you are the ones you have to run from. You follow Nika and Madison, two Indigenous women who find themselves in a terrifying spot after a fight with a cop goes wrong. One was just trying to protect the other, but now the law sees them as criminals. The movie feels like a high-stakes chase that puts you right in the passenger seat. It captures that feeling of panic and friendship perfectly, making you root for these two girls from the very first scene. 

The acting is where this movie really shines because the chemistry between the leads feels totally real. You will love how the tension builds up, though some parts in the middle feel a bit slow. If you like stories about fighting the system and loyal friends, you have to see this. It looks amazing in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but if you are a collector, you should definitely add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best picture quality. Otherwise, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to catch it this weekend.
endingExplained: At the end, Nika and Madison are cornered in a small town. A surprise witness comes forward with video footage that proves the police officer started the fight. This clears their names just in time. Instead of going to jail, they are seen as victims of police brutality. The movie ends with them finally safe at home, showing that the truth came out, though they are still scarred by the whole experience.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gripping chase stories and strong character dramas.
